definition: In computer vision and image processing, a feature is a piece of information about the content of an image; typically about whether a certain region of the image has certain properties.
details: Features may be specific structures in the image such as points, edges or objects. Features may also be the result of a general neighborhood operation or feature detection applied to the image. Other examples of features are related to motion in image sequences, or to shapes defined in terms of curves or boundaries between different image regions. More broadly a feature is any piece of information that is relevant for solving the computational task related to a certain application. This is the same sense as feature in machine learning and pattern recognition generally, though image processing has a very sophisticated collection of features. The feature concept is very general and the choice of features in a particular computer vision system may be highly dependent on the specific problem at hand.

explainer.lead: A feature is a useful clue extracted from an image, such as a point, edge, shape, or sign of motion. It gives a computer something relevant to work with when solving a visual task, but the right clues depend on the application.

tiers.eli5: A feature is like a clue you use to solve a picture puzzle. You might notice a corner, a line, or the outline of an object instead of studying every tiny part of the picture. A computer can use clues like these to understand images and how things move through a sequence of pictures.
tiers.practitioner: A practitioner selects features according to the task, using image structures or the results of neighborhood operations and feature detection. Points, edges, objects, curves, region boundaries, and motion in image sequences can all serve as features. Because the concept is so broad, a feature set that works for one computer vision system may not suit another problem.
tiers.paperLevel: For an image I and region R, a feature can be written as f(I, R): information indicating whether R has specified properties, or more generally any information relevant to the computational task. It may describe an image structure directly or result from a neighborhood operation or feature detection. The definition is highly general, so it does not prescribe a universal representation or guarantee that a chosen feature will be useful across applications.

explainer.example: To separate a dark mug from a light table, a system can detect the edge where the image changes between the two regions. Following that edge produces a boundary that describes the mug’s outline, providing a feature relevant to identifying or isolating it.

usedIn.name: Image processing
usedIn.detail: Uses points, edges, and other detected structures as information about image content.

usedIn.name: Shape analysis
usedIn.detail: Uses curves and boundaries between image regions to describe shapes.

usedIn.name: Motion analysis
usedIn.detail: Uses features related to movement across image sequences.

explainer.intuition: An image contains far more raw information than a particular task may need. A feature picks out a relevant property or structure, turning part of that content into a useful clue.
howItWorks: Start with an image or an image sequence.
Consider a region, neighborhood, curve, boundary, or change over time.
Identify a structure or apply feature detection or a neighborhood operation.
Use the resulting information if it is relevant to the application’s task.
explainer.whyItMatters: Features connect image content to computational tasks by supplying task-relevant information. Their generality allows computer vision systems to work with structures ranging from simple edges to objects, shapes, and motion.
misconceptions: A feature is not necessarily a complete object; it can be a point, edge, curve, boundary, or motion-related property.
There is no single best set of features, because the choice depends heavily on the problem.
A feature need not be directly visible as a structure; it can also result from feature detection or a neighborhood operation.
